paper_main_claim: ChatGPT's stories may be generated from a nested hierarchy of probability distributions (story/segment/sentence/token)
paper_method: Prompt ChatGPT with a story, ask for retelling with changed protagonist/antagonist, compare old vs new
paper_key_result: Changes propagate locally, proportional to character difference; some story segments (e.g. Disturbance) stay stable, others change
paper_conclusion: ChatGPT's behavior must be analyzed on three levels: surface behavior, middle-level probability hierarchy, bottom-level transformer machine
student_takeaway: Benzon's black-box narrative probing parallels Haralick-Ramesh performance characterization; both perturb inputs and measure what's preserved
student_contribution: Ran a mini replication of Benzon's character-substitution experiments and a quantitative analogue using Markov sequences with bit-flip noise
student_critique: Benzon's approach is qualitative/single-example and lacks controls (session history, model version); proposes making it rigorous via multiple trials, controlled parameters, and statistical testing
